title: Does early network bursting predict how an untreated human iPSC well settles? A replication on the lab's developmental plates (REAL data, Kapucu 2022)
status: registered before any windowed feature was computed on the developmental plates
origin: an exploratory, post hoc look at D35's human wells (48-well baseline, DIV29) found two settling behaviours: wells that keep falling after the first five minutes and wells that recover. Network-burst rate in the first window predicted the later trend (Spearman -0.73, 24 wells), synchrony less so (-0.49), firing rate not at all (-0.02); in rat wells none of the three did (+0.17, +0.12, -0.04). That analysis is not registered; this registration tests it on independent recordings.
seen_before_registration: the exploratory result above, computed in a scratch script on the 48-well baselines (hPSC_MEA3Baseline_DIV29, Rat_MEA2Baseline_DIV22)

everything in hpsc_split_half (D32), including its replication pool on these developmental plates: per-recording split-half changes of every feature and their SDs, 144 usable human recordings from 12 wells and 58 rat recordings from 12 wells, and that network-burst rate was unscored for 50 human developmental recordings because their first half had no network bursts
no feature of any window shorter than half a recording on the developmental plates
data: the D32 replication pool exactly: hPSC_MEA1 and hPSC_MEA2 (12-well, 10-min recordings) at DIV28 or later, Rat_MEA1 (12-well, 10-min) at DIV21 or later, NoTreatment wells, the recordings D32 judged usable

method.windows: each recording cut into 6 consecutive windows of equal length (100 s for these 10-min recordings), cut as in D32 and D35
method.early_state: features/mea.py extract_features at defaults on window 0 alone: nb0 = network_burst_rate_per_min, sync0 = synchrony_index, mfr0 = mfr_hz; an undefined value (no active electrode in the window) leaves the recording unscored for that feature, and the count is reported
method.late_trend: per recording, the firing rate per window on the electrodes active over the whole recording (as D35), y_k = log2 of it with D35's floor, and late_b = ordinary least-squares slope of y_k on k for k = 1..5
method.statistic: Spearman rho between an early-state feature and late_b over all usable recordings of a species, pooled across ages
method.interval: 95% percentile interval from 2,000 bootstrap resamples of wells (all of a well's recordings together) within species, seed 20261028

N1_early_network_bursting_predicts_settl.statement: in human iPSC recordings, more network bursting in the first window goes with a more negative later trend
N1_early_network_bursting_predicts_settl.test: pass if the 95% interval of rho(nb0, late_b) in human recordings lies below 0; fail otherwise

N2_not_in_rat.statement: rat recordings show no such negative relation
N2_not_in_rat.test: pass if the 95% interval of rho(nb0, late_b) in rat recordings does not lie entirely below 0; fail otherwise

N3_network_state_not_firing_rate.statement: in human recordings the early network state predicts the later trend better than the early firing rate does
N3_network_state_not_firing_rate.test: pass if the 95% interval of rho(mfr0, late_b) - rho(nb0, late_b) in human recordings lies above 0; fail otherwise

uninterpretable: a prediction is uninterpretable if its species has fewer than 30 scored recordings from at least 8 wells, or (N1, N3) if nb0 is zero in more than 80% of scored human recordings

reported_not_tested.sync0: rho(sync0, late_b) per species with its interval
reported_not_tested.primary_pool_post_hoc: the exploratory result on the 48-well baselines recomputed by the module, labelled post hoc

assumption_check.assumption: the relation is not an artefact of culture age (both network bursting and settling may change with age)
assumption_check.check: rho(nb0, late_b) after regressing the ranks of both on DIV (partial Spearman), and the median of per-DIV rhos, both reported for each species; if the partial rho in human recordings is above -0.1, the report says the N1 relation may be an age effect

reporting: all three predictions reported with values whatever the outcome
